subject: Batch window throughput cliff during settlement window — urgent exec escalation
messages:
From: Luke Harper <luke.harper@clearbridge-payments.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:12:14 -0700
Subject: Production window alert — throughput collapse during 09:00–09:30 PST

Priya / David,

We're seeing a sustained throughput drop (~60%) and a spike in 5xx errors starting at 09:03 PT during our settlement window. Token queues are piling up and several jobs are timing out. This is impacting settlement runs for multiple merchants; we have an active backlog.

Attached is a short snapshot of the error wave and a token-utilization chart. The errors appear correlated to long-context batch requests from our overnight batch job that started earlier today.

Can Redwood confirm whether our reserved capacity is being throttled or if there is noisy neighbor behavior? We need a quick mitigation plan — either immediate burst authorization or a fallback route to keep settlements on time.

Luke
Head of Ops
ClearBridge Payments
[Attachment: clearbridge_error_snapshot.png (png)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:28:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production window alert — throughput collapse during 09:00–09:30 PST

Thanks for the flag, Luke — we see the same spike. Putting an immediate ops/eng triage on this. Initial read: dedicated GPU pool for your reservation is saturated by a mix of long-context batched inference and a recent change in request batching from your side that increased average sequence length.

Immediate asks / plan (next 30–90 mins):
- Naomi: can you open a 3p bridge and authorize a temporary 2x burst into our shared pool for 2 hours? That should relieve the queue while we profile.
- Aditya: can your team verify kernel selection / batch sizing for the affected model and check whether KV-cache fragmentation is causing extra memory pressure?
- David / Marissa: we will likely need an exec sign-off for the burst plus a one-time credit to cover the overage if the shared pool use is required. Please confirm cost estimate.

Attachments: I pushed the reservations export for your reservation (see reservations_report_Q4.csv) — contains headroom history and reservation configs.

I will keep Luke updated on the bridge link.

—Priya
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reservations_report_Q4.csv (csv)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:40:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production window alert — throughput collapse during 09:00–09:30 PST

On it — quick triage below.

What we observed:
- Dedicated pool for ClearBridge (reservation ID DB-6482) reached sustained GPU utilization >95% from 09:03–09:18 PT.
- Telemetry shows a sharp increase in average sequence length from ClearBridge's batch job (median went from ~512 tokens to ~1,800 tokens).
- OOMs are rare but scheduling latency increased; preemption queued requests and caused a cascade of 5xx repeated attempts.

Short-term mitigation (implemented at 09:45 PT):
- Authorized a temporary policy change to allow ClearBridge to spill up to 2x of their reserved throughput into the shared pool for the next 2 hours.
- Applied a conservative per-request token cap (max_sequence_override = 2,000) to reduce sudden outliers.
- Restarted a subset of the scheduling daemons on the pool to clear stuck tasks.

Notes / blockers:
- The shared pool route will increase cost for Redwood; recommend exec approval for a one-time credit (~$2.6k estimated) and explicit written permission from ClearBridge to proceed.
- Need Eng confirmation on kernel path inefficiency for long sequences (Aditya).

Bridge link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/incident/ISR-1092

—Naomi
Sr. Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, CEO <ceo@redwood.com>, FinanceOps <finance@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 10:05:57 -07:00
Subject: Request: Burst authorization & one-time credit for ClearBridge (DB-6482) — approval needed by 11:00 PT

Marissa / team,

Summary: ClearBridge (DB-6482) experienced a reserved-capacity throughput collapse during their 09:00–09:30 PT settlement run. Ops authorized a temporary spill into the shared pool to prevent missed settlements. Estimated incremental cost: $2,600 for the two-hour spill. Customer impact: delayed settlements if not mitigated; reputational/SLAs at risk.

Proposed ask:
1) Exec approval to absorb the incremental shared-pool cost as a one-time goodwill credit to ClearBridge (FinanceOps, please approve).
2) Authorization for continued spill for up to 4 hours if required while Eng completes profiling and a config rollback is staged.

Rationale: avoiding a failed settlement window prevents downstream reconciliation work and preserves the account (high strategic value). Deal impact: ClearBridge is in active renewal; preservation of revenue tightly bound to on-time settlements.

Please reply with: APPROVE / DENY by 11:00 PT. If APPROVE, FinanceOps will post the credit and Naomi will keep the spill open until the handoff.

Thanks —
David
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Luke Harper <luke.harper@clearbridge-payments.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 16:22:09 -07:00
Subject: Re: Batch window throughput cliff during settlement window — urgent exec escalation

Thanks for the quick triage and the temporary spill — that minimized the impact. We accept the one-time credit approach while we work on reducing our average sequence length (we have a change queued to batch smaller payloads for the next run).

We would like a postmortem that includes: root cause, action items to prevent recurrence (config or model sizing recommendations), and confirmation of the reservation changes once complete.

FWIW, our procurement team has requested a small, permanent reservation tweak to better match our settled batch profile — I copied contracts on this thread.

Luke
Head of Ops
ClearBridge Payments
